title: CQRS Pattern
description: Learn the Command Query Responsibility Segregation pattern for separating read and write operations.

data.text: Command Query Responsibility Segregation (CQRS) separates read and write operations into different models. Netflix, Amazon, and financial systems use CQRS to optimize reads and writes independently, enabling complex query capabilities without impacting write performance.

In traditional CRUD, the same model handles reads and writes. In CQRS, commands (writes) use a task-based model, and queries (reads) use a separate, optimized read model. The two models are synchronized through events.

CQRS is often combined with event sourcing. The write side stores events; the read side builds denormalized projections. This separation enables each side to scale independently and use different database technologies.

data.title: CQRS Benefits
items: Optimized read models for complex queries
Independent scaling of read and write workloads
Flexible read models (NoSQL, search engines, caches)
Enables complex reporting without affecting writes

data.title: CQRS Complexity
data.text: CQRS adds significant complexity. Do not use it for simple CRUD applications. Use it when you have complex queries that cannot be efficiently served from a normalized write model.

data.title: Example: CQRS for Order Management
data.code: Write side uses normalized SQL; read side uses denormalized document store.

# Write side (Command Model)
# - PostgreSQL with normalized tables
# - Handles OrderCreated, OrderShipped commands
# - Emits OrderCreated, OrderShipped events

# Read side (Query Model)
# - MongoDB with denormalized documents
# - OrderHistory projection:
# {
#   orderId: 'ord-789',
#   customerName: 'Alice',
#   items: [
#     { productName: 'Widget', quantity: 2 }
#   ],
#   shippingStatus: 'shipped',
#   trackingNumber: '1Z999'
# }

data.caption: CQRS architecture
data.definition:
graph LR
    C[Command] --> W[Write Model]
    W -->|Events| ES[Event Store]
    ES -->|Projection| RM[Read Model]
    Q[Query] --> RM
    RM -->|Optimized for reads| C

items.question: Do I need event sourcing to use CQRS?
items.answer: No. You can use CQRS without event sourcing by having the write model publish events directly to the read model. Event sourcing is often combined with CQRS but is not required.

items.question: How do I keep read and write models in sync?
items.answer: Use an event bus. The write side publishes events; the read side consumes them and updates its projections.

items.question: What database should I use for the read model?
items.answer: Choose based on your query patterns. Use Elasticsearch for full-text search, MongoDB for document queries, or Redis for caching.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: CQRS separates read and write models
Enables independent optimization of reads and writes
Adds complexity; use only when needed
data.takeaway: CQRS is a powerful pattern for complex domains but should not be used for simple CRUD applications.
